_comment: Tool policy for the self-briefing planner quartermaster.sh runs unattended.
The planner's prompt embeds a Linear ticket description — text any
workspace member can edit — and runs with nobody watching, so the policy
is deny-by-default and the allow list is deliberately tiny: everything
absent from `allow` fails immediately rather than prompting, so nothing
blocks waiting for a human who is asleep.
No Bash at all. Permission patterns match the head of a command line and
cannot see what it goes on to execute or write: an allow-listed find can
-exec anything, rg can --pre anything, and cat/jq can redirect anywhere,
which would hand a poisoned description exactly the shell a deny list
pretends to close. Research is Read/Grep/Glob; nothing more is needed to
write a brief.
No Task either. A subagent is a second context with a turn budget of its
own — the ration --max-turns exists to impose, handed out again — and it
reads the same description with none of the caller's suspicion. Whatever
a subagent could research, the planner can research itself.
There is deliberately no file-write rule here, and adding one back would
be a mistake. The planner writes its brief into a scratch directory that
quartermaster.sh creates per call and hands it as its working directory;
acceptEdits permits writes inside that tree, and the harness copies the
result out. A rule cannot express this — the path is minted per call — and
a rule is not what confines the write anyway: Claude Code refuses edits
outside the session's cwd tree, and refuses edits under ~/.claude entirely
as a protected path, whatever this file says. Those two walls are why the
old Write(~/.claude/harness/runs/**) rule could never work: runs/ lives
under ~/.claude, so every self-brief failed as 'planner wrote no brief',
silently, from the day it shipped until 2026-08-10. Spelling it Edit(path)
instead does not help — the wall is the path, not the tool name — though
note if you ever do add a file rule that only Edit rules are consulted by
file permission checks and a bare Edit in deny would cover Write too.
The planner's write reach is now one empty scratch dir rather than all of
runs/, which is strictly tighter than what this file used to ask for. What
it gives up is nothing: quartermaster.sh asks for a uniquely named,
non-armable candidate, publishes it with an atomic no-clobber link, and
checkpoints every brief.md before the planner starts so it can quarantine
and restore writes elsewhere — and 'elsewhere' is now unreachable anyway.
The deny list below is belt to those braces: a rule added to allow later
cannot re-open the shell or network paths without also deleting a deny.
The harness's own secrets are denied by path. The planner has no way to
send anything anywhere itself — the network tools are denied above — but
the brief it writes is read by an implementer whose settings do allow Bash
and WebFetch, so a secret quoted into a brief is a secret one step from
leaving the machine. These paths assume the default HARNESS_DIR; a key
kept elsewhere (LINEAR_API_KEY_FILE) needs its own deny.
Read is what this closes. Grep and Glob take a search root rather than a
file path and are matched by tool name only, so treat the deny as the
brake it is, not as proof — what confines the planner is that nothing it
reads has a way out of this machine.
